blocks.text: Lesson 7 gave you one triangle of place-endings — -ssa/illative/-sta — for being inside, going into, and coming out of a container-like place. Finnish has a second triangle for surfaces and, importantly, for people: -lla, -lle, -lta. This is also how Finnish says 'I have', and how reviewers describe money moving to or from them.

blocks.title: Money moves 'from' you, literally
blocks.text: Where English says 'I was charged', Finnish says minulta veloitettiin — literally 'from me it was charged'. The money is pictured leaving you, grammatically, even though you're the passive party. This ablative-plus-passive combination is extremely common across the price complaints in this corpus.

blocks.content: {-lla|grammar|adessive suffix|on/at} (or -llä after front vowels) marks being on a surface or, with people, 'at/by' that person. Finnish reuses this exact ending to express possession: there's no separate verb for 'to have' — instead you say [person]-lla on [thing], literally 'at [person] is [thing]'. {Minulla|grammar|adessive, 1st person|at me / I have} on auto — 'I have a car'.

items.fi: {Korjaamolla|grammar|adessive|at the repair shop} oli hyvä maine.
items.en: The repair shop had a good reputation.
My friend has the same car.

blocks.content: {-lta|grammar|ablative suffix|from} (or -ltä) marks 'from', specifically moving away from a person or a surface — the exact mirror of -lla. Minulta veloitettiin, 'charged from me'. You also saw this back in Lesson 1: apu löytyi kaverilta, 'help was found from a friend'.

items.en: I was overcharged (charged too much from me).
I heard about it from a friend.

blocks.title: The third corner of the triangle
blocks.text: {-lle|grammar|allative suffix|to/onto} completes the set: movement toward a person or surface. Soitettiin minulle, 'I was called' (literally 'it was called to me'). Same three-way pattern as Lesson 7's container triangle — just built for people and surfaces instead of rooms and buildings: minulla (at me), minulle (to me), minulta (from me).

items.en: I was called the next day.
A price estimate was given to me in advance.

lines.speaker: A
lines.en: Do you have a car being repaired?

lines.speaker: B
lines.fi: On. Minulta veloitettiin 161 euroa, mutta korjaamolta ei kuulunut mitään sen jälkeen.
lines.en: Yes. I was charged 161 euros, but I didn't hear anything from the repair shop after that.

lines.speaker: B
lines.en: No. I had to call them myself.

blocks.title: Paul Noble Rule
blocks.text: Picture two triangles now: Lesson 7's -ssa/illative/-sta for rooms and containers, and today's -lla/-lle/-lta for surfaces and people. Same three directions — staying, arriving, leaving — just aimed at a different kind of noun. If the noun is a place you go inside, use Lesson 7's set. If it's a person, a surface, or possession, use today's.

blocks.content: Minulta: MI-nul-ta (three even syllables, stress on MI). Minulla: MI-nul-la (nearly identical to minulta — listen closely for -lla vs -lta at the end, the meaning flips). Minulle: MI-nul-le (same root, third ending).

blocks.title: What you now own
items: minulla on — I have, Finnish's way of expressing possession without a 'to have' verb
the second case triangle: -lla (at), -lle (to), -lta (from), for people and surfaces
you can now read minulta veloitettiin and similar money-and-person constructions correctly
you can tell Lesson 7's container triangle apart from this lesson's people/surface triangle
you can say what you have, who gave you something, and who you heard something from
